_comment: Aspendora fork addition (Vikunja CIPP-30). Abused top-level domains used by the TLD block templates (Config/TenantAllowBlockListTemplates/AbusedTlds-*.json) and the ListTldExposure audit. Keep the templates in step with this list; backend/Tests/Email/AbusedTldTemplates.Tests.ps1 fails if they drift. senderRisk/urlRisk = false-positive risk for US SMB clients (Low / Medium / High).
sources: Interisle Consulting 'Phishing Landscape' 2023-2025 (new gTLD and Freenom ccTLD abuse)
Microsoft Learn: tenant-allow-block-list-email-spoof-configure (*.TLD sender syntax) and tenant-allow-block-list-urls-configure (*.TLD/* URL syntax)

tlds.note: Google gTLD that looks like a file extension. Almost no mail is sent from .zip domains, but a URL block can match plain-text file names such as 'report.zip' in a message body, and Microsoft may refuse *.zip/* as a file extension. URL block is in its own template.
Same issue as .zip ('clip.mov' in body text). URL block is in its own template.
Consistently in the top abused gTLDs. A few legitimate APAC suppliers and some marketing link domains use it.
Cheap and heavily abused, but also used by real startups, crypto/web3 vendors and some SaaS (e.g. abc.xyz). Check ListTldExposure before enforcing.
Abused for phishing landing pages; some email service providers and link shorteners use .click tracking domains, so the URL block can catch marketing mail.
High abuse rate, little legitimate US business use.
